content.jointProblem: Can a self-supervised, contrastive representation learned from a site's unlabelled Modbus/BACnet traffic characterise normal behaviour well enough to flag anomalous flows and behaviour drift, and can the resulting score be explained to a plant manager in plain language without any labelled attack examples? The first experiment tests whether flow- and packet-level features from ProtoSense captures can be tokenised and modelled with the researcher's missingness- and time-gap-aware self-supervised pipeline, evaluated against operator-verified normal periods and controlled testbed injections.

rationale.text: Her core line of work is learning useful representations from industrial logs with no labelled examples, which matches the company's zero-attack-example constraint directly.

sources.quote: can learn meaningful latent representations from such logs without any labelled examples
TabSCL is evaluated on seven datasets from manufacturing and utilities sectors

rationale.text: Her time-aware contrastive objective has been evaluated specifically on downstream anomaly detection, the exact task ProtoSense needs.

sources.quote: improved downstream anomaly detection AUROC by an average of 4.3 percentage points over a standard fixed-window contrastive baseline

rationale.text: She treats missingness and non-uniform sampling as first-class design elements rather than an imputation afterthought, which suits packet captures with gaps and event-driven logging.

sources.quote: a missingness-aware feature tokeniser that encodes observed/unobserved status as part of the token embedding
with missing rates between 12 % and 58 % per channel

rationale.text: She has already built deployment-time drift monitoring for tracking representation quality after model handover, which corresponds to the company's need to flag drift from a site baseline.

sources.quote: development of lightweight deployment-time drift monitors for tracking representation quality after model handover

rationale.text: Her projects include taking these representations onto constrained edge hardware, relevant to on-device inference on an appliance.

sources.quote: including the TabSCL framework and its deployment onto edge hardware

rationale.text: She has a track record of building benchmark datasets jointly with regional industrial partners and is explicitly open to company projects on self-supervised pipelines for industrial data.

sources.quote: developed benchmark datasets in partnership with three manufacturing companies in Vojvodina
contract research on self-supervised or contrastive learning pipelines for industrial data

constraints.text: The method must operate without any labelled malicious traffic; supervised training on public ICS datasets is not acceptable, since that approach already produced unusable false-positive rates in the field.

sources.quote: we have zero examples of malicious traffic and supervised classifiers are useless to us
it flagged so many false positives in real deployments that clients started switching the alerts off

constraints.text: Every alert must be explainable to a plant manager in plain language, so the anomaly score needs an accompanying human-readable justification.

sources.quote: we can explain to a plant manager in plain language

constraints.text: Inference must run on the appliance itself, on the planned variant with a dedicated security processor, without degrading packet forwarding latency.

sources.quote: a fifth hardware variant in late 2025 with a dedicated security processor to support on-device anomaly detection without affecting packet forwarding latency

constraints.text: The work depends on client traffic archives, the hardware bench and the existing firmware codebase, all shared under NDA, so data-sharing, anonymisation and client-consent terms must be settled before any modelling.

sources.quote: access to our traffic archives, our hardware bench, and our existing firmware codebase under NDA
we have collected several terabytes of captures from consenting clients over the past three years

constraints.text: The researcher's working precondition is at least six months of historical logs from the industrial partner.

sources.quote: industrial partner can share at least six months of historical sensor logs

constraints.text: Capacity is tight on both sides: the company can release only one to two engineers part-time, and only one doctoral student is available for a secondment of up to three months, while the researcher's own availability is unknown.

sources.quote: We can dedicate one to two engineers part-time to a collaborative project
available for secondment to an NTP company for up to three months from mid-2025

risks: Transfer gap: all of her cited anomaly-detection evidence comes from process/SCADA sensor logs and tabular sensor datasets, not from network packet captures; whether Modbus/BACnet flow and packet features behave like her sparse tabular sensor streams is untested and must be the first experiment.

Evaluation without labels: with no confirmed attack captures, true detection performance cannot be measured directly; only operator-confirmed normal periods and testbed-injected traffic can serve as a proxy, and this limits how strongly any result can be claimed.

Explainability is not evidenced in her material: her publications report representation quality, AUROC and F1, but nothing on producing plain-language explanations, so the plant-manager-facing requirement is a genuine open problem.

Alert fatigue repeats the earlier failure: the company's clients already switched off alerts once; a per-site baseline that drifts or is over-sensitive could end the same way, and per-site retraining on terabytes of captures may be needed for each customer.
Her cross-domain transfer evidence is qualified, which matters for a product shipped to many different sites with heterogeneous networks.

Her own availability is unknown, and the only committed student resource is a three-month secondment, which may be too short for a multi-site, multi-year capture study; company engineering support is part-time only.

Data access depends on client consent and NDA terms; some clients with twenty years of unmonitored operation may be unwilling to release packet captures, and the captures may contain sensitive operational detail.
questions: Can ArmaturaSec provide flow-level or packet-level feature exports from ProtoSense with documented semantics, rather than only raw pcap, and who defines the feature schema?

Is any traffic available that is known or strongly suspected to be malicious (incident reports, red-team exercises, testbed injection with physical PLC simulators) for validation, even if not part of the training data?
What is the target hardware profile and latency budget for on-device inference, and is the dedicated-security-processor variant available on the bench now?
What false-alarm rate do clients actually tolerate before switching alerts off, and how quickly must a new site baseline be learned from that site's traffic?
What form of explanation is acceptable to a plant manager — per-alert contributing features, a drift score, or a narrative summary — and has this been tested with end users?
What are the NDA, anonymisation and client-consent conditions for sharing three years of captures, and which clients have agreed?
What is the researcher's actual availability, and is the intended arrangement a joint project, an industrial PhD, or a combination with the ADAPT-ICS student secondment?
Who funds the work and for how long, given one to two part-time company engineers and a three-month student secondment?
